name: District of Columbia
stateTaxAgencyName: DC Office of Tax and Revenue
dueDateNotes: DC follows the federal schedule: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15. If a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.
selfEmploymentNotes: The District of Columbia applies a seven-bracket graduated tax (4% to 10.75%) to your federal AGI after DC's own standard deduction. Starting in 2025, DC decoupled from the federal standard deduction and set its own amounts: $15,000 single, $30,000 married, $22,500 head of household. Single and married filers use the same brackets. This page is written for DC residents — DC cannot tax the wages of non-resident commuters.
uniqueFacts: DC decoupled from the federal standard deduction for 2025, setting its own amounts ($15,000 single / $30,000 married) rather than following the larger federal figures.
DC has no commuter tax — federal law bars the District from taxing the income of people who work in DC but live in Maryland or Virginia, so this calculator is for DC residents.
DC's top rate of 10.75% on income over $1 million is one of the highest state-level rates in the country, and its brackets have been unchanged since 2022.
